stem: When examining a child suspected of having Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) conjunctivitis, what is the significance of using fluorescein staining?

options.text: To identify the presence of a branching dendritic ulcer on the cornea.
To detect the presence of Trantas dots at the limbus.
To determine if the discharge is mucoid or purulent in nature.
To visualize the depth of an alkali chemical burn.

explanation: Fluorescein stains areas of epithelial loss, revealing the characteristic dendritic ulcer found in HSV keratitis.
rationale: This stain helps highlight specific patterns of damage on the clear front surface of the eye.

optionExplanations.A: Fluorescein stains areas of epithelial loss, revealing the characteristic dendritic ulcer found in HSV keratitis.
optionExplanations.B: Trantas dots are signs of allergic conjunctivitis and are visible without staining; they are not used to diagnose HSV.
optionExplanations.C: The nature of the discharge is determined through clinical observation and history, not through fluorescein staining.
optionExplanations.D: While staining might be used in trauma, its primary diagnostic utility in the HSV context is identifying specific epithelial ulcer patterns.

source.hint: This stain helps highlight specific patterns of damage on the clear front surface of the eye.
